synthesis: Fourier support acts as a common analytic resource parameter in three distinct parts of the argument: under contour motion it controls the exponential growth of the complex-shifted test function and hence the residue and terminal-line errors; in the local expansion it decides whether frequency one can contribute a visible 1/log X term; and in the odd-prime contribution it sets the cutoff Y = X^sigma whose length must be offset by character-sum cancellation. Comparing the Jutila and Poisson treatments further shows that changing the cancellation machinery changes the resulting error-versus-support tradeoff.
source_support: Unit u08 bounds a vertical shift of g by X^(sigma w) and obtains support-dependent errors from critical-zero residues and the shifted contour. Unit u10 derives a coefficient multiplying the Fourier transform of g at 1 and states that this secondary term is present only when support exceeds (-1,1). Unit u12 turns p^(2l+1) <= X^sigma into a Jutila/Cauchy-Schwarz error X^(-(1-sigma)/2) times logarithms, while unit u13 sets Y = X^sigma and, after smoothing, squarefree splitting, Poisson summation, and frequency-class estimates, obtains a different support-dependent error for the specified family.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis identifies the same support radius with three different operational quantities across the parent units: vertical-shift growth, access to the boundary frequency 1, and primal character-sum length. It then contrasts two distinct cancellation mechanisms on that support-controlled length, rather than merely grouping sections that mention support.
limits: The calculations occupy different regimes and cannot be combined into one uniform theorem: u08 assumes RH and sigma < 1, u10 explicitly allows sigma > 1, and u13 uses a particular dyadic odd squarefree family plus external Gao lemmas. The displayed thresholds are task-, method-, target-error-, and family-dependent; they are not intrinsic impossibility boundaries, and exact exponents and constants remain formula-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because four distinct parent units jointly establish a concrete dependency that no one unit supplies alone: support is converted into contour growth, frequency visibility, and summation length, and the two odd-sum units exhibit how different analytic inputs alter the resulting bound. The source explicitly supplies each bridge, while the synthesis preserves the incompatible regimes and conditional assumptions.
